newsitem.title: CHINA: Profits of China's metals industry slide in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Profits of China's metals industry slide in 1996.

text.p: Total pre-tax profits of firms directly under the control of China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp fell 47 percent year-on-year to 3.15 billion yuan in 1996, state media said on Wednesday.
Total post-tax profits of the firms dipped by 2.265 billion yuan in 1996 compared with 1995, the official Economic Information Daily said. It did not give the actual net profit figure for 1996.
Chinese metals officials attributed the decline in profits partly to weak domestic prices and also on poor management of nonferrous metals enterprises, it said.
Officials said the industry should curb poor investment and duplication of facilities in 1997, limit expansion of smelters and the processing sector.

The state-owned giant accounts for most of China's output of non-ferrous metals. Its output of nonferrous metals, including copper, lead, zinc and aluminium, was estimated at more than 4.45 million tonnes in 1996, up 6.5 percent from 1995.
